summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, multiple kidney and pancreas transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and chronic heart failure was admitted for severe weakness and hypotension. She had recently completed treatment for E. coli bacteremia. Evaluation revealed cardiogenic shock likely due to volume overload and demand ischemia, with elevated cardiac enzymes but no acute coronary syndrome. She was supported with norepinephrine, which was weaned as her blood pressure stabilized. Anemia was managed with transfusions and increased erythropoietin. Her heart failure improved with fluid removal via peritoneal dialysis. Hand tremors resolved during the stay, and her thyroid function remained suboptimal but stable on levothyroxine. She completed her course of meropenem with no evidence of ongoing infection. She was discharged to extended care with medication adjustments including increased tacrolimus, new vitamin B12, and adjusted warfarin, along with plans for outpatient follow-up in infectious disease, dermatology, and primary care.
